annotations.text:
FinHive Loan Manager — MVP2
React + Chakra UI, dark theme.

Status hues carried forward exactly from MVP1's dark_config.json (Active #025c33, Overdue #6b0307, Pending #804001, Paidoff #022a52), re-tinted for legibility on a dark ground. Amber #e0a336 is the new brand accent and marks everything agent-originated.

Type: IBM Plex Sans + IBM Plex Mono (tabular figures for money and reference IDs).

The ReAct trace is the product, not a loading state.

Step 2 is the whole argument for an agent over a search box: 'sharma group' is not a stored value, so the model resolves it to sharma_traders BEFORE querying. A naive implementation would filter on the raw string, return zero rows, and confidently say 'no loans found'.

Token count, cost and latency are shown per turn — this is the metering substrate for the eval harness.

The safety gate. The agent never writes to the loans table.

Every mutating tool writes a proposal row instead. The diff is rendered from stored before/after JSONB snapshots — never from the agent's prose description of what it did.

Only the owner role sees Approve, enforced server-side by Postgres RLS rather than by hiding a button. The batch applies in one transaction.

Row 3 shows the inline date-edit state. MVP1's most defect-dense area was filter state and date handling — three architectural rewrites — so the filter chips deliberately show applied state as a single visible source of truth, and the footer restates the filtered totals so a wrong filter is obvious rather than silent.
